technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as an extension of the existing Spring XD-style architecture, using Spring Security for authentication, authorization, roles, and ACL enforcement.
Represent security definitions and resource permissions as external configuration with secure defaults, preserving backward compatibility for existing deployments.
Use method- and service-level authorization as the authoritative enforcement point, with consistent checks exposed to the REST API, DSL Shell, and Admin UI.
Implement the Python processor as a stream processor using a subprocess bridge over standard input/output, with a documented message serialization format and lifecycle management.
Implement the R processor using an external-process integration model rather than requiring native R libraries in the JVM, to reduce platform-specific deployment constraints.
Implement the Hive sink using the existing Hadoop/Hive client APIs and Spring XD sink conventions, supporting configurable Hive connection, database, table, and serialization settings.
Upgrade Spring Core to version 4.1.1 while preserving the existing dependency-management strategy and resolving transitive dependency conflicts through targeted compatibility changes.
Include unit, component, integration, security, and regression tests for each user story, with mocked external Python, R, Hadoop, and Hive dependencies where practical.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD codebase, build, deployment model, REST API, DSL Shell, and Admin UI are available and reasonably buildable before implementation begins.

The increment targets a Java 17-compatible environment only where required by the stated Spring Framework context; legacy project constraints may require compatibility adjustments during the Spring Core upgrade.
The existing authentication mechanism can be extended with Spring Security and does not require implementing a new identity provider, user directory, OAuth provider, or certificate authority.
SSL/HTTPS configuration covers documenting and wiring server certificate, key, trust, and enablement properties; obtaining or managing certificates is out of scope.
Basic authentication applies to administration endpoints and uses the existing user store or configured authentication provider.
Security definitions identify REST/API entities and operations and support group/role-based access decisions; a new administrative policy editor is not required.
ACLs cover stream lifecycle and read/view operations for DSL Shell and Admin UI resources, with backward-compatible permissive defaults where no policy is configured.
Python and R processors exchange records through a documented line-oriented or framed standard-input/standard-output protocol and do not require arbitrary in-process execution.
Python and R runtime installation, operating-system packaging, specialized native libraries, and production-scale performance tuning are limited to configuration guidance and integration tests.
The Hive sink supports the primary expected append/write use case and does not include a full Hive metastore administration interface, schema evolution framework, or advanced transaction semantics.
The Spring Core upgrade is limited to version 4.1.1 and directly related dependency and compatibility changes; unrelated framework upgrades are excluded.

Effort estimates include implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, local integration testing, documentation, and build verification, but exclude elapsed waiting time and external stakeholder approval.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build, security flow, REST resources, DSL Shell commands, Admin UI, processor and sink extension points, and dependency management. Produce the detailed implementation approach and identify compatibility risks.

Add or verify administration endpoint configuration for HTTPS and Basic authentication, connect it to the existing server and security setup, provide secure defaults, and add configuration and endpoint tests.

Design and implement configurable entity- and REST-operation security definitions, role/group matching, policy loading and validation, authorization service interfaces, error handling, and unit/component tests.

Map DSL Shell operations such as create, destroy, and view streams to protected resources; integrate ACL checks into command execution and service calls; preserve permissive defaults; and add authorization and command-level tests.

Integrate the shared authorization model with Admin UI-backed REST calls and UI operation visibility or denial behavior for stream creation, destruction, and viewing. Add client/server integration tests and error handling.

Investigate Java integration alternatives, select and implement the standard-input/standard-output subprocess approach, define message and error protocols, manage process startup and shutdown, expose processor configuration, and add mocked-runtime and end-to-end tests.

Evaluate rJava, Renjin, and external-process options against the Spring XD model; implement the selected R processor integration, including record conversion, process lifecycle, configuration, failure handling, documentation, and integration tests.

Implement a configurable Hive sink using the existing sink extension conventions and Hadoop/Hive client APIs, including connection and table settings, record serialization, write/error behavior, lifecycle management, and tests with mocked or embedded-compatible dependencies.
Update dependency management to Spring Core 4.1.1, resolve transitive version conflicts, adapt incompatible code or tests, verify SpEL-related behavior, and run module-level regression tests.

Run the complete build and test suite, add cross-feature scenarios covering authentication, security definitions, ACLs, REST, DSL Shell, UI, processors, Hive, and the dependency upgrade, and fix integration and compatibility defects.

Document HTTPS and Basic authentication configuration, security definitions, ACL syntax and defaults, Python and R runtime requirements and examples, Hive sink configuration, upgrade notes, and representative usage scenarios.
Update build descriptors, dependency exclusions, configuration templates, packaging metadata, sample resources, CI execution, installation verification, and release-quality change review.
